```{r echo=FALSE}
df.raw <- read.csv("Life Expectancy Data.csv")
df <- na.omit(df.raw)

log_cols <- c(
  "thinness.5.9.years",
  "thinness.1.19.years",
  "Population",
  "GDP",
  "HIV.AIDS",
  "under.five.deaths",
  "Measles",
  "percentage.expenditure",
  "infant.deaths"
)
for (col in log_cols) {
  df[[col]] <- log1p(df[[col]])
}

drop_cols <- c(
  "Country",              
  "infant.deaths",        
  "percentage.expenditure",
  "thinness.5.9.years"    
)
df[drop_cols] <- NULL

df.numeric <- df[, sapply(df, is.numeric)]
```


### Import and Data Manipulation

The data was imported from the `Life Expectancy Data.csv` file, and NAs were removed using `na.omit`. The columns chosen for log transform were transformed, and the columns to be dropped were dropped (outlined in [Exploratory]). All remaining numeric columns were plotted against `Life.expectancy` to verify correct import and transformation. The clean data is named `df`.

```{r echo=FALSE}
par(mfrow=c(2, 2))

for (column_name in names(df.numeric)) {
    plot(df.numeric[[column_name]],
       df$Life.expectancy,
       xlab = column_name,
       ylab = "Life Expectancy")
}
```


### Train-Test split

The cleaned and transformed data (`df`) is split into training and testing using random selection with a set seed for reproducibility.
```{r echo=FALSE}
set.seed(67)

n        <- nrow(df)
train_idx <- sample(n, size = floor(0.7 * n))
train_df  <- df[train_idx, ]
test_df   <- df[-train_idx, ]
```

### Model fitting and selection
First a full model was fitted, including all the predictors:

```{r full-model}
lm.full <- lm(Life.expectancy ~ ., data = train_df)
lm.full$coefficients
```
